adventure.title: The Lantern in the Marsh
adventure.summary: Hook: a green lantern appears on the marsh every seventh night. Truth: Iselde, the lamplighter's daughter, crossed seven years ago and is now bound to the lantern on the island. Goal: reach the island and decide her fate.

scenes.title: The Last Ferry
scenes.purpose: The party learns of the lantern and has to choose whether to cross tonight.
scenes.wayOut: Across the water after the lantern, or back to the ferry house.
scenes.description: A flat-bottomed ferry creaks across black water. On the far bank, a single green lantern sways where no house should be.
scenes.notes:
- **Brannoc** refuses to cross after dark unless paid double.
- **Seventh night**: he knows the lantern only appears then.

scenes.title: The Ferry House
scenes.purpose: The party finds out who crossed seven years ago.
scenes.wayOut: Back to the ferry and after the lantern.
scenes.description: A damp one-room hut with a smoking stove and a logbook of every crossing for forty years.
scenes.notes:
- **Logbook** shows a passenger who crossed seven years ago and never returned.
- **Iselde**, the lamplighter's daughter, is that passenger.

exits.label: Go after the lantern after all

scenes.title: The Sunken Causeway
scenes.purpose: The marsh tests the party on the way to the island.
scenes.wayOut: Ends on the island shore once the eels flee or the party gets past them.
scenes.description: Stepping stones half under water. Something large moves beneath the reeds.

battleMap.notes:
- **Night**: the lantern on the island gives dim light.
- **Deep water** off the stones: swimming costs double movement.
- **Eels** hide in the reeds and drag characters off the stones.

scenes.title: The Lamplighter's Island
scenes.purpose: The party decides what becomes of Iselde.
scenes.wayOut: The adventure ends with the lantern broken or carried to the ferry.
scenes.description: A ruined tower with a lantern that burns without oil. A pale figure tends it.
scenes.notes:
- **Iselde** is bound to the lantern.
- **Breaking it** frees her but angers the marsh.
- **Carrying it** to the ferry lets her rest.

npcs.name: Old Brannoc
npcs.voice: Gravelly and slow, clears his throat before bad news, calls everyone "traveller".

npcs.name: Iselde
npcs.voice: A breathy whisper, trails off mid-sentence, repeats the last word she heard.

items.name: Ferry Logbook
items.description: Forty years of crossings in cramped handwriting. One entry is circled in red ink.

monsters.name: Reed Stalker

traits.name: Hold Breath
traits.text: The stalker can hold its breath for 1 hour.

traits.name: Murky Ambush
traits.text: The stalker has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks while it is in muddy water or among reeds.

actions.name: Bite
actions.text: Melee Attack Roll: +4, reach 5 ft. 6 (1d8 + 2) Piercing damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, the stalker pulls it 5 feet toward deeper water.

monsters.notes:
- **Ambush predator**: waits below the causeway.
- **Lets go** of anyone who hurts it badly.

monsterPool.name: Marsh Eel
monsterPool.description: A thick, mottled eel as long as a rowing boat.

clues.text: Iselde crossed to the marsh seven years ago and never came back.

leads.text: Logbook: her name is the last entry, with no return crossing.
Witness: Brannoc remembers the girl who never came back.

clues.text: The lantern only appears every seventh night.

leads.text: Witness: Brannoc counts the nights on his fingers and says it only ever comes on the seventh.
Logbook: crossings to the marsh are marked with a green dot, always seven nights apart.

puzzles.title: The Tower Door
puzzles.prompt: The tower door has no handle. Seven stone lamps are carved in a ring around it, each with an empty wick hole. Six of them bear notches, one to six; the lowest bears a wave instead. Above the door: “Count the nights as the ferryman does, and light the one that waits.”
puzzles.solution: Light the lamp with the wave: it stands for the seventh night, when the lantern appears. The door swings open without a sound.

hints.text: The notches under the lamps count something.
The lantern appears every seventh night.
Six lamps have notches. The seventh is marked by the river instead.

puzzles.notes:
- **Wrong lamp**: green smoke, and the marsh whispers Iselde's name; nothing worse.
- **Giving up**: Iselde opens the door from inside as soon as someone calls her by name.
